newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada spot gas higher again as supply tightens.
newsitem.headline: Canada spot gas higher again as supply tightens.

text.p: Canadian spot natgas prices for May climbed again on Wednesday as buyers scrambled for supply and NOVA's intra-Alberta pipeline network continued to operate below its target linepack, traders said.

Spot gas at the AECO storage hub in Alberta was discussed in the low C$1.90s per gigajoule range, up about a dime from Tuesday and almost 20 cents from last week. One-month gas was quoted at C$1.83/1.84 per GJ.
"It's totally supply-driven," a Calgary trader said of the surprising surge. He said a growing number of seasonal gas plant turnarounds should support prices over the coming weeks.
Storage injections into Alberta facilities were said to be in the 200 million cubic feet a day range, a figure marketers said was unusually low for the time of year.

Prices were also strong at export and domestic points in British Columbia. At Sumas, gas was talked in the high US$1.40s per million British thermal units, up from US$1.30/1.35 on Tuesday and US$1.23/1.28 last week. Westcoast compressor station 2 was also sharply higher.
"It's being driven by Alberta," said a trader of B.C. gas. "But I'm not sure where the gas is going -- it's not going into storage."
In Manitoba, site of TransCanada PipeLines Ltd's Station 41 outside Winnipeg, severe flooding had yet to impact the company's system, a TransCanada spokesman said.
He said dikes around the compressor station, from which gas heads to either eastern Canada or the U.S. border, were strengthened, he said.
